rule: Ruchaka: Mars in a kendra in its own or exaltation sign; set aside when Mars is combust
text: Ruchaka is formed because Mars stands in a kendra (the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th house) in Mesha, Vrishchika or its exaltation sign Makara. It is one of the five Mahapurusha yogas, each built on one planet at full strength in an angle. Ruchaka is read for physical drive, initiative and the readiness to lead and compete; the house it falls in shows where that drive is most visible. A combust Mars does not form it.

rule: Bhadra: Mercury in a kendra in its own or exaltation sign; set aside when Mercury is combust
text: Bhadra is formed because Mercury stands in a kendra in Mithuna or in Kanya, which is both its own and its exaltation sign. It is the Mercury member of the five Mahapurusha yogas. Bhadra is read for a quick, orderly mind, skill with words, numbers and trade, and an ability to learn by watching. The house holding Mercury shows the field where this shows most. A combust Mercury does not form it.

rule: Hamsa: Jupiter in a kendra in its own or exaltation sign; set aside when Jupiter is combust
text: Hamsa is formed because Jupiter stands in a kendra in Dhanu, Meena or its exaltation sign Karka. It is the Jupiter member of the five Mahapurusha yogas. Hamsa is read for a steady moral sense, a liking for learning and teaching, and respect that comes from conduct rather than position. The house it occupies shows where this is lived out. A combust Jupiter does not form it.

rule: Malavya: Venus in a kendra in its own or exaltation sign; set aside when Venus is combust
text: Malavya is formed because Venus stands in a kendra in Vrishabha, Tula or its exaltation sign Meena. It is the Venus member of the five Mahapurusha yogas. Malavya is read for an eye for beauty and comfort, warmth in relationships and a taste for the arts and good company. The house holding Venus shows the area where these matter most. A combust Venus does not form it.

rule: Sasa: Saturn in a kendra in its own or exaltation sign; set aside when Saturn is combust
text: Sasa is formed because Saturn stands in a kendra in Makara, Kumbha or its exaltation sign Tula. It is the Saturn member of the five Mahapurusha yogas. Sasa is read for endurance, patience with slow work, and authority built through responsibility and service to many. The house that holds Saturn shows where the long effort is made. A combust Saturn does not form it.

rule: Gaja Kesari: Jupiter in a kendra from the Moon; set aside when Jupiter is combust or debilitated
text: Gaja Kesari is formed because Jupiter stands in a kendra (the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th sign) counted from the Moon. The elephant and lion of its name stand for the Moon's feeling and Jupiter's judgement working together. It is read for sound sense, a good name among one's people and the ability to recover from setbacks. The rule asks for a Jupiter that is neither combust nor debilitated.

rule: Budhaditya: the Sun and Mercury in the same sign
text: Budhaditya is formed because the Sun and Mercury share one sign. Mercury never moves far from the Sun, so this is a common yoga, and the classical texts read it for a clear intellect, skill in speech and writing, and a mind that organises what it sees. When Mercury is combust in the same sign, the yoga still forms but the Mercury row carries its own combust tag.

rule: Chandra-Mangala: the Moon and Mars in the same sign
text: Chandra-Mangala is formed because the Moon and Mars share one sign. Saravali reads the pairing of feeling and drive for earning through one's own effort and for a forthright manner in dealings. The sign and house in which the two meet show the area of life where this energy is spent. It is a simple conjunction yoga with no cancellation rule.

rule: Sunapha: a planet other than the Sun and the nodes in the 2nd from the Moon, with the 12th empty
text: Sunapha is formed because one or more planets (not the Sun, Rahu or Ketu) stand in the 2nd sign from the Moon while the 12th from the Moon is empty of such planets. It belongs to the lunar yogas that describe the Moon's neighbours. Sunapha is read for self-earned means and a settled position; the planet that forms it colours the reading, Jupiter for learning, Venus for comforts, Saturn for steady work.

rule: Anapha: a planet other than the Sun and the nodes in the 12th from the Moon, with the 2nd empty
text: Anapha is formed because one or more planets (not the Sun, Rahu or Ketu) stand in the 12th sign from the Moon while the 2nd from the Moon is empty of such planets. It belongs to the lunar yogas. Anapha is read for a composed manner, steady habits and a liking for quiet and reflection, with the planet that forms it adding its own flavour to the picture.

rule: Durudhara: planets other than the Sun and the nodes on both sides of the Moon (2nd and 12th)
text: Durudhara is formed because planets (not the Sun, Rahu or Ketu) stand both in the 2nd and in the 12th sign from the Moon, so the Moon is held on both sides. It belongs to the lunar yogas. Durudhara is read for support from others, means that come from more than one direction and a generous disposition. The two flanking planets name the kinds of support involved.

rule: Kemadruma: no planet other than the Sun and the nodes in the 2nd or 12th from the Moon; cancelled by a planet with the Moon, in a kendra from the Moon or in a kendra from the Lagna
text: Kemadruma is formed because no planet other than the Sun, Rahu or Ketu stands in the 2nd or the 12th sign from the Moon, leaving the Moon without neighbours. The classical reading is a tendency to feel unsupported and to depend on one's own resources. The texts give three cancellations: a planet sharing the Moon's sign, a planet in a kendra from the Moon, or a planet in a kendra from the Lagna; when one applies, the row reads cancelled.

rule: Vesi: a planet other than the Moon and the nodes in the 2nd from the Sun, with the 12th empty
text: Vesi is formed because one or more planets (not the Moon, Rahu or Ketu) stand in the 2nd sign from the Sun while the 12th from the Sun is empty of such planets. It belongs to the solar yogas that describe the Sun's neighbours. Vesi is read for even temper, truthful speech and a steady outlook; a benefic forming it is read more warmly than a malefic.

rule: Vasi: a planet other than the Moon and the nodes in the 12th from the Sun, with the 2nd empty
text: Vasi is formed because one or more planets (not the Moon, Rahu or Ketu) stand in the 12th sign from the Sun while the 2nd from the Sun is empty of such planets. It belongs to the solar yogas. Vasi is read for skill, memory and a liking for work done behind the scenes; the planet that forms it gives the reading its particular colour.

rule: Ubhayachari: planets other than the Moon and the nodes on both sides of the Sun (2nd and 12th)
text: Ubhayachari is formed because planets (not the Moon, Rahu or Ketu) stand both in the 2nd and in the 12th sign from the Sun, so the Sun is flanked on both sides. It belongs to the solar yogas. Ubhayachari is read for balance between effort and ease, a broad circle of acquaintance and standing that is recognised by others. The flanking planets name the sources.

rule: Adhi: Mercury, Jupiter and Venus all in the 6th, 7th or 8th from the Moon
text: Adhi yoga is formed because the three natural benefics Mercury, Jupiter and Venus all stand in the 6th, 7th or 8th sign counted from the Moon. It is one of the lunar yogas and is rarer than the Sunapha family because it needs all three benefics together. Adhi is read for responsibility that is willingly given, good standing among colleagues and a capacity to carry others.

rule: Vasumati: Mercury, Jupiter and Venus all in upachaya houses (3, 6, 10, 11) from the Lagna or from the Moon
text: Vasumati is formed because the natural benefics Mercury, Jupiter and Venus all stand in upachaya houses (the 3rd, 6th, 10th or 11th), counted from the Lagna or all counted from the Moon. The upachaya houses are the growing houses, so the yoga is read for resources that build with time and effort rather than arriving at once. The Why? inputs name which reference point was used.

rule: Amala: a natural benefic in the 10th from the Lagna or from the Moon
text: Amala is formed because a natural benefic (Mercury, Jupiter or Venus) stands in the 10th house from the Lagna or in the 10th sign from the Moon. The name means spotless, and the yoga is read for a clean reputation in work and public life and for conduct that others trust. The benefic that forms it suggests the manner, Jupiter through fairness, Venus through grace, Mercury through skill.

rule: Saraswati: Jupiter, Venus and Mercury each in a kendra, trikona or the 2nd house, with Jupiter in own, exaltation or friendly sign
text: Saraswati is formed because Jupiter, Venus and Mercury each stand in a kendra, a trikona or the 2nd house, and Jupiter is in its own, its exaltation or a friend's sign. Named for the goddess of learning, it is read for ease with language, study, music and the arts, and for being sought out for one's knowledge. It needs the Lagna, so it is not evaluated in Moon-chart mode.

rule: Lakshmi: the 9th lord in own or exaltation sign in a kendra or trikona, with the Lagna lord neither debilitated nor combust
text: Lakshmi yoga is formed because the lord of the 9th house stands in its own or exaltation sign in a kendra or trikona while the Lagna lord is neither debilitated nor combust. The 9th is the house of fortune and the Lagna lord carries the native, so the yoga is read for means that come with good conduct and for a settled, respected life. It needs the Lagna and is not evaluated in Moon-chart mode.

rule: Shakata: Jupiter in the 6th, 8th or 12th from the Moon; cancelled when Jupiter is in a kendra from the Lagna
text: Shakata is formed because Jupiter stands in the 6th, 8th or 12th sign counted from the Moon, the places where its support for the mind is read as least available. The name means cart, and the classical picture is of fortune that rises and falls in turns. When Jupiter also stands in a kendra from the Lagna the yoga is cancelled and the row says so with the cancelling rule.

rule: Guru-Chandala: Jupiter in the same sign as Rahu or Ketu
text: Guru-Chandala is formed because Jupiter shares a sign with Rahu or with Ketu. The pairing of the teacher planet with a node is read for unconventional beliefs, learning that comes from outside the usual channels and a tendency to question received authority. Which node is involved, and the sign and house of the meeting, give the reading its direction. There is no cancellation rule.

rule: Kala Sarpa: all seven planets on one side of the Rahu–Ketu axis, none sharing a node's sign (Rahu to Ketu); type by Rahu's house
text: Kala Sarpa is formed because all seven planets from the Sun to Saturn lie within the half of the zodiac that runs from Rahu towards Ketu, with none sharing a node's sign. The texts read it for a life whose themes are strongly shaped by the Rahu–Ketu axis, often with a marked shift in direction around mid-life. Its type is named from the house Rahu occupies, which the Why? inputs list.

rule: Kala Amrita: the reversed Kala Sarpa, all seven planets on the Ketu-to-Rahu side of the axis
text: Kala Amrita is the reversed form of Kala Sarpa, formed because all seven planets lie within the half of the zodiac that runs from Ketu towards Rahu, with none sharing a node's sign. Many astrologers read this direction as the gentler of the two, with the themes of the axis unfolding through release rather than pursuit. The type takes the number of Rahu's house, listed in the Why? inputs.

rule: Neecha Bhanga Raja: a debilitated planet whose fall is cancelled by the debilitation-sign lord or exaltation-sign lord in a kendra, by the planet itself in a kendra, or by exchange with its sign lord
text: Neecha Bhanga Raja yoga is formed because a debilitated planet has its fall cancelled: the lord of its debilitation sign or of its exaltation sign stands in a kendra from the Lagna or the Moon, or the planet itself does, or it exchanges signs with the lord of the sign it occupies. The classical reading is of a weakness that is turned into a strength through circumstance and effort. The inputs name the planet and the reasons.

rule: Harsha (Vipreet Raja): the 6th lord in the 6th, 8th or 12th house
text: Harsha is formed because the lord of the 6th house stands in a dusthana, the 6th, 8th or 12th house. It is the first of the three Vipreet Raja yogas, in which a lord of a difficult house sits in another difficult house and the two are read as cancelling each other. Harsha is read for gains through handling competition, debt and obstacles well, and for strength that comes from facing problems directly.

rule: Sarala (Vipreet Raja): the 8th lord in the 6th, 8th or 12th house
text: Sarala is formed because the lord of the 8th house stands in a dusthana, the 6th, 8th or 12th house. It is the second Vipreet Raja yoga, named for straightness. It is read for the ability to stay steady through upheaval, for research and depth, and for benefit that arrives from matters others find difficult. The house that holds the 8th lord shows where this is tested.

rule: Vimala (Vipreet Raja): the 12th lord in the 6th, 8th or 12th house
text: Vimala is formed because the lord of the 12th house stands in a dusthana, the 6th, 8th or 12th house. It is the third Vipreet Raja yoga, named for purity. It is read for measured spending, contentment with what one has and a life that gains from distance, retreat or foreign places. The house holding the 12th lord shows where the restraint is practised.

rule: Dhana: the 2nd and 11th lords conjunct, in exchange or in mutual aspect
text: This Dhana yoga is formed because the lords of the 2nd house (what is held) and the 11th house (what is gained) are joined, exchanged or in mutual aspect by Parashara's full aspects. Linking the two wealth houses is the simplest of the classical Dhana yogas and is read for income and savings that support each other. The Why? inputs name the two lords and the kind of link.

rule: Raja yoga: a kendra lord and a trikona lord conjunct or in exchange (every pair listed)
text: A Raja yoga is formed because the lord of a kendra (the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th) and the lord of a trikona (the 5th or 9th) share a sign or exchange signs. Parashara calls the kendras the Vishnu houses and the trikonas as the Lakshmi houses, so their lords meeting is read for standing, support and achievement in the areas the two houses govern. Every such pair in the chart is listed in the inputs.

rule: Dharma-Karmadhipati: the 9th and 10th lords conjunct or in exchange
text: Dharma-Karmadhipati yoga is formed because the lords of the 9th house (dharma, fortune, teachers) and the 10th house (karma, work, standing) share a sign or exchange signs. Parashara counts this the strongest of the Raja yogas because it joins the best trikona with the best kendra. It is read for work that matches one's values and for recognition earned through it. The sign holding the two lords is listed.

rule: Parivartana: two planets each in the sign the other rules; Maha, Khala or Dainya by the houses exchanged; all-Dainya shown as cancelled
text: Parivartana is formed because two planets each occupy the sign the other rules, binding their two houses together. It is called Maha Parivartana when both houses are among the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 7th, 9th, 10th and 11th, Khala when one is the 3rd, and Dainya when one is a dusthana (6th, 8th or 12th). Every exchange in the chart is listed with its kind; when all of them are Dainya the row reads cancelled.

rule: Kemadruma cancelled: a planet other than the Moon and the nodes in the 4th, 7th or 10th from the Moon
text: Kemadruma is cancelled in this chart because a planet other than the Moon, Rahu or Ketu stands in a kendra counted from the Moon, in the 4th, 7th or 10th sign. Phaladeepika gives this as one of the three classical cancellations: the Moon lacks immediate neighbours, but it is held by a planet at an angle, so the sense of being without support does not apply. The Why? inputs name the planet.

rule: Kemadruma cancelled: a planet other than the Moon and the nodes in a kendra from the Lagna
text: Kemadruma is cancelled in this chart because a planet other than the Moon, Rahu or Ketu stands in a kendra from the Lagna, in the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th house. Jataka Parijata counts an angular planet from the Lagna as enough to hold the chart together even when the Moon stands alone. This cancellation needs a known birth time, so it is not applied in Moon-chart mode. The inputs list the planet.

rule: Kemadruma cancelled: a planet other than the Sun and the nodes shares the Moon's sign
text: Kemadruma is cancelled in this chart because a planet other than the Sun, Rahu or Ketu shares the Moon's own sign. The yoga describes a Moon without company in the 2nd and 12th, and a planet standing with the Moon itself is the most direct form of company the texts accept. Phaladeepika lists this as the first of the three cancellations. The Why? inputs name the planet with the Moon.

rule: Gaja Kesari set aside: the forming Jupiter is combust or debilitated
text: Gaja Kesari is present by position but set aside in this chart because the Jupiter that forms it is combust (too close to the Sun) or in its debilitation sign Makara. The yoga asks for a Jupiter able to lend its judgement to the Moon, and the classical reading is that a weakened Jupiter cannot do so fully. The row therefore reads cancelled, with Jupiter's dignity and combustion state listed in the inputs.

rule: Shakata cancelled: Jupiter in a kendra from the Lagna
text: Shakata is cancelled in this chart because Jupiter, although it stands in the 6th, 8th or 12th sign from the Moon, also stands in a kendra from the Lagna, in the 1st, 4th, 7th or 10th house. Phaladeepika gives this as the standard exception: an angular Jupiter supports the chart as a whole even when it is far from the Moon. The cancellation needs a known birth time.

rule: Mahapurusha yoga set aside: the forming planet is combust
text: This Mahapurusha yoga is present by position but set aside because the planet that forms it is combust, within the classical orb of the Sun. Parashara's rule asks for a planet in a kendra in its own or exaltation sign with its strength intact, and combustion is read as the Sun overpowering that strength. The row shows the house, sign and dignity so the near miss is visible rather than hidden.

rule: Parivartana shown as cancelled: every exchange involves the 6th, 8th or 12th house (Dainya)
text: The exchange in this chart is of the Dainya kind, because one of the two exchanged houses is a dusthana, the 6th, 8th or 12th. Dainya Parivartana is traditionally read as a link that brings the difficulties of the dusthana into the other house, so it is listed as cancelled rather than as a formed yoga. The inputs list each exchange with its kind, so a Maha or Khala exchange elsewhere in the chart stays visible.

rule: No named yoga of the checked list is formed in this chart
text: None of the named yogas this app checks is formed in this chart, and none is present in a cancelled state. That is common and says nothing against the chart: the yoga list is a set of classical patterns, not a measure of quality, and most of what a chart shows lives in the planet table, the houses and the dashas. The Why? inputs list every yoga that was checked so the result can be traced.
